question: Which suture type naturally breaks down inside the body over time?
explanation: Absorbable sutures are designed to be broken down and absorbed by body tissues, meaning they do not need to be pulled out manually. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why are monofilament sutures often preferred to reduce the risk of infection?

options.A: They never require tying secure knots during a surgical repair
options.B: They stimulate rapid blood flow directly to the wound edges
options.C: They dissolve much faster than any other available material
options.D: They feature a single smooth strand that bacteria cannot easily hide in

explanation: A single smooth strand leaves fewer microscopic gaps or spaces where microorganisms can cling and multiply compared to braided threads. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h1)

question: How long should a newly sutured wound ideally be kept clean and dry after repair?

options.B: Until the patient finishes all meals
options.D: Only during the first six hours

explanation: Keeping the wound dry during the initial forty-eight hours helps prevent moisture from introducing bacteria into the fresh closure. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the best way for a mother to dry her perineal suture line after a gentle wash?

options.A: Rub the stitches hard with a rough towel
options.B: Pat the area gently with a clean, soft cloth
options.C: Use a hot hair dryer on the highest setting
options.D: Leave the area completely wet without touching

explanation: Patting avoids pulling or adding friction to the delicate healing tissue, whereas rubbing can break open the fresh wound edges. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a classic sign of a healing wound becoming infected?

options.A: Spreading redness and warmth in the area
options.B: Pus or foul-smelling fluid draining out
options.C: A cool, pale skin surface around the stitches
options.D: Worsening pain several days after repair

explanation: Infection typically causes increased blood flow, warmth, and inflammation rather than a cool, pale appearance. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h3)

question: What does the term wound dehiscence mean in clinical practice?

options.A: The edges of the repaired wound pull apart prematurely
options.B: New skin grows too fast over the top of the thread
options.C: The suture material dissolves inside the body too early
options.D: A hard knot forms underneath the surface of the skin

explanation: Dehiscence happens when the closed wound edges separate or pop open before the underlying tissue has gained enough strength to hold itself together. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why are facial sutures typically removed much sooner than sutures on the legs?

options.A: Facial thread material always dissolves on its own anyway
options.B: Leg muscles move constantly and push the threads out
options.C: Facial skin heals faster and experiences lower physical tension
options.D: Patients complain louder about stitches on their face

explanation: The face has a rich blood supply supporting rapid healing, and removing facial stitches early helps prevent permanent mark formation from the thread tracks. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h4)

question: A patient has non-absorbable stitches over her knee joint following a fall. When should the midwife plan to remove them?
explanation: Areas crossing joints endure constant stretching and movement, requiring extra time for the skin edges to gain enough strength before stitches come out. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why must a midwife cut the suture thread close to the skin surface during removal?

options.A: To prevent pulling contaminated surface thread through the tissue track
options.B: To ensure the scissors remain sharp enough for the next procedure
options.C: To make sure the discarded thread stays long enough to reuse later
options.D: To prevent the patient from feeling any cold air on the wound

explanation: The exposed part of the thread collects bacteria from the air and skin surface; pulling that dirty section through the flesh can seed an infection. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of using dissecting forceps during suture removal?

options.A: To scrub away stubborn dried blood from the wound edges
options.B: To measure the exact length of the scar after healing
options.C: To gently lift the knot so the scissors can reach the thread
options.D: To inject local anesthetic pain medication into the skin

explanation: Forceps provide a secure grip to elevate the suture knot slightly above the skin level without causing trauma to surrounding tissue. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h5)

question: In which direction should a midwife pull the cut thread when sliding it out of the skin?

options.A: Away from the wound toward the outer healthy skin
options.B: Straight up toward the ceiling with a sharp jerk
options.C: Toward the wound line to keep the edges closed
options.D: In a fast circular motion to loosen stubborn knots

explanation: Pulling toward the wound pushes the edges together, preventing the newly sealed skin from tearing open again during extraction. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h6)

question: What critical final action must a midwife take after pulling out all the stitches?

options.A: Scrub the bare skin vigorously with a stiff brush
options.B: Prescribe a strong course of oral antibiotics
options.C: Apply tight pressure bandages for twenty-four hours
options.D: Count the removed pieces to ensure nothing is left behind

explanation: Counting ensures that no small fragment of suture material remains trapped inside the tissue, which would trigger an inflammatory foreign body reaction. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h6)

question: Why should a midwife advise a patient to protect a recently unsutured wound from tight clothing?

options.A: Pressure from clothing causes the skin to grow extra hair
options.B: Fabric dyes will permanently stain the healing scar dark blue
options.C: Friction from tight garments can irritate and break fragile new skin
options.D: Tight cloth stops blood from reaching the deep organs inside

explanation: Newly closed skin lacks the toughness of mature tissue and can easily chafe, blister, or tear when rubbed by tight fabrics. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h7)

question: What important warning should a midwife give a patient regarding her scar after suture removal?

options.A: The wound will completely disappear within forty-eight hours
options.B: She can safely scrub the area with soap immediately
options.C: The scar tissue takes several months to reach full strength
options.D: No further skin care or protection is ever needed

explanation: Newly healed skin is initially weak, and telling the patient about the gradual strengthening process helps her protect the site properly. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T5#BMP120_U3_T5_h7)
